experiment: Native cross-layer + accumulated-within design test in deployment (refuted)
setup: SEER serving sim, Llama-3.1-8B, mooncake, ctx4096, N16, new48, measured-DMA

cross_dominant_probe.note: cross-dominant scorer (w=[5,40,0,0]) keeping prev-layer top-r gets eps 0.647 >> H2O 0.500; the cross signal is a WORSE predictor of the current masked oracle than H2O accumulation

findings: Native cross-layer indicator (true prev-layer top-r, free at decode) gives NO deployment improvement (xqpnative==xqp); plumbing verified active (native ON/OFF differ 0.0001).
H2O-style accumulated within feature gives NO improvement either (xqpfull==xqp).
H2O beats every learned variant at every budget.

ROOT CAUSE: the offline label (future top-r by FULL attention, h4) and the deployment oracle (current top-B_t by MASKED attention) are DIFFERENT targets. The 2-view wins offline (+0.10 recall@10%) on the former; H2O wins deployment on the latter because its running accumulation directly tracks current heavy-hitters.

METHODOLOGICAL TAKEAWAY: offline saliency-prediction accuracy does NOT predict deployment selection quality at block granularity — a model can win every offline metric and still lose to a trivial heavy-hitter in the loop.

future_aware_test.method: bin per_step_eps by k = step % decision_period(8); does learned eps degrade slower with lookahead than H2O?
future_aware_test.verdict: REFUTED — H2O wins at every lookahead k; neither degrades within the 8-step window because intra-generation drift is mild (salient set stable). No predictive-eviction advantage exists to exploit.

overall_verdict: Three design hypotheses (horizon-lookahead, native-cross/accum-within, future-aware-eviction) all CLEANLY REFUTED. At block granularity, reactive H2O is near-optimal in deployment; no learned selector beats it because mild within-generation drift makes the salient set stable. The honest contribution is the measurement/benchmark + this rigorous negative, not a selector that beats H2O.
